title: Separating what Matchday knows from what it copies
items: A headline accuracy figure says almost nothing about a prediction model that usually names the same side as the betting market: on those games it simply inherits the market's record.

The published record is now split in two. On the 80.9% of graded picks where Matchday agreed with the market it hit 54.0%. On the 19.1% where it went its own way it hit 41.5%, against 58.5% for the side the market preferred.

Judged on the quality of its stated probabilities rather than its picks, Matchday is not measurably worse than the market — the comparison interval still contains zero on the games with full market prices.
Both readings are published as they are. The disagreement sample is still small enough that it is a strong hint rather than a settled verdict, and it is labelled that way.
